qti-assessment-item.title: Calculate boot recognition and deferred adjusted basis on IRC Section 1031 real property exchanges using Form 8824 rules.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_1): Calculate boot recognition and deferred adjusted basis on IRC Section 1031 real property exchanges using Form 8824 rules.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A CPA's client transfers relinquished rental real estate (FMV 900,000 dollars, adjusted basis 500,000 dollars, mortgage 250,000 dollars) via a Qualified Intermediary and acquires replacement real estate (FMV 920,000 dollars, new mortgage 310,000 dollars), receiving 40,000 dollars cash at closing. What recognized gain must be reported on Form 8824?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: 0 dollars because new mortgage debt of 310,000 dollars exceeds the 250,000 dollar mortgage given up by more than 40,000 dollars
40,000 dollars because cash boot received cannot be netted against excess mortgage liability assumed
290,000 dollars equal to gross mortgage relief of 250,000 dollars plus 40,000 dollars cash received
400,000 dollars equal to the entire realized gain on the relinquished property

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: Excess mortgage liability assumed (60,000 dollars) never offsets actual cash boot received under Treas. Reg. 1.1031(d)-2.
Verified: Realized gain is 400,000 dollars; debt relief (250,000) is fully offset by new debt assumed (310,000), leaving 40,000 dollars of taxable cash boot recognized.
Diagnostic rationale: Mortgage relief of 250,000 dollars is offset by the 310,000 dollar replacement mortgage assumed.
Diagnostic rationale: Partial boot causes recognition only up to net boot received (40,000 dollars), leaving 360,000 dollars deferred.

qti-assessment-item.title: Calculate boot recognition and deferred adjusted basis on IRC Section 1031 real property exchanges using Form 8824 rules.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_1): Calculate boot recognition and deferred adjusted basis on IRC Section 1031 real property exchanges using Form 8824 rules.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: If a Section 1031 taxpayer transfers relinquished real property on October 20 of Year 1 and does not extend their calendar-year individual Form 1040 (due April 15 of Year 2), when does the statutory exchange completion period expire?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: April 18 of Year 2, because the taxpayer always receives a full 180 calendar days
April 15 of Year 2, because IRC Section 1031(a)(3)(B) caps the window at the unextended tax return due date
December 4 of Year 1, because both identification and closing must occur within 45 days
October 15 of Year 2 automatically, even without filing Form 4868

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: 180 days from October 20 falls after April 15, so the earlier return due date cap controls unless Form 4868 is timely filed.
Verified: IRC Section 1031(a)(3)(B) terminates the exchange period on the earlier of 180 days after transfer or the due date (including extensions) of the transferor's return.
Diagnostic rationale: December 4 is the 45-day identification deadline, not the closing deadline.
Diagnostic rationale: The October 15 extended window applies only if the taxpayer actually files a valid extension before filing the Year 1 return.

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply IRC Section 108 insolvency exclusions and Form 982 tax-attribute reduction ordering to cancelled recourse debt.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_2): Apply IRC Section 108 insolvency exclusions and Form 982 tax-attribute reduction ordering to cancelled recourse debt.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: An individual taxpayer outside bankruptcy has 900,000 dollars in total liabilities and 760,000 dollars in total asset fair market value immediately before a lender cancels 200,000 dollars of recourse business debt. How much COD income is excluded under IRC Section 108(a)(1)(B)?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: 200,000 dollars because any pre-discharge insolvency excludes the entire debt cancellation
140,000 dollars excluded on Form 982, with the remaining 60,000 dollars recognized as ordinary COD income
0 dollars because insolvency exclusion applies only inside a formal Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing
760,000 dollars capped at total asset fair market value

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: IRC Section 108(a)(3) strictly caps the insolvency exclusion at the dollar amount by which the taxpayer is insolvent immediately before discharge.
Verified: Pre-discharge insolvency equals 140,000 dollars (900,000 minus 760,000), excluding 140,000 dollars on Form 982 and leaving 60,000 dollars taxable.
Diagnostic rationale: IRC Section 108(a)(1)(B) provides a standalone non-bankruptcy insolvency exclusion up to the insolvency amount.
Diagnostic rationale: The statutory cap is the insolvency excess (140,000 dollars), not gross asset value.

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply IRC Section 108 insolvency exclusions and Form 982 tax-attribute reduction ordering to cancelled recourse debt.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_2): Apply IRC Section 108 insolvency exclusions and Form 982 tax-attribute reduction ordering to cancelled recourse debt.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Absent an affirmative IRC Section 108(b)(5) election to reduce depreciable property basis first, which tax attribute must be reduced first on Form 982 following an IRC Section 108 insolvency exclusion?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Adjusted basis of personal-use residences and investment land
Net operating losses (NOLs) for the taxable year of discharge and any NOL carryovers
Foreign tax credit carryovers to or from the taxable year of discharge
Passive activity loss and credit carryovers under IRC Section 469

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: Property basis reduction occurs fifth in the statutory sequence unless a Section 108(b)(5) depreciable-property election is made.
Verified: IRC Section 108(b)(2)(A) places current-year net operating losses and NOL carryovers first in the mandatory attribute-reduction order.
Diagnostic rationale: Foreign tax credit carryovers sit seventh (last) in the IRC Section 108(b)(2) sequence.
Diagnostic rationale: Passive activity carryovers sit sixth in the IRC Section 108(b)(2) sequence.

qti-assessment-item.title: Differentiate tax realization rules for recourse versus nonrecourse foreclosures and IRC Section 1041 divorce transfers.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_3): Differentiate tax realization rules for recourse versus nonrecourse foreclosures and IRC Section 1041 divorce transfers.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A lender forecloses on a rental building (FMV 620,000 dollars, adjusted basis 540,000 dollars) securing 750,000 dollars of nonrecourse debt, and separately a spouse transfers marital stock (FMV 300,000 dollars, basis 110,000 dollars) to an ex-spouse under a divorce decree. Which tax treatment applies?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: The nonrecourse foreclosure yields 210,000 dollars of Section 1001 gain with 0 COD income, and the divorce transfer recognizes 0 gain with a 110,000 dollar carryover basis
The nonrecourse foreclosure yields 80,000 dollars of capital gain plus 130,000 dollars of COD income, and the divorce transfer triggers 190,000 dollars of capital gain
Both transactions qualify for full tax-free exclusion under IRC Section 108(a)(1)
The nonrecourse foreclosure yields 130,000 dollars of deductible ordinary loss, and the ex-spouse takes a stepped-up 300,000 dollar basis

qti-content-body.p: Verified: Under Tufts, nonrecourse foreclosure amount realized equals the full 750,000 dollar debt (750,000 minus 540,000 = 210,000 gain, 0 COD), while IRC Section 1041 mandates zero gain and carryover basis (110,000) on divorce transfers.
Diagnostic rationale: Bifurcation at FMV applies only to recourse debt, and IRC Section 1041(a) prevents gain recognition on divorce transfers.
Diagnostic rationale: Neither nonrecourse Tufts gain nor Section 1041 carryover transfers fall under IRC Section 108.
Diagnostic rationale: Extinguishing 750,000 dollars of debt against 540,000 dollars of basis produces gain, and Section 1041(b) prohibits basis step-up.
